cells.tense: The pen is in your hand, and you are writing this in the present, with the ones who share it.
cells.act: calibrate what you say to what can be heard
cells.ask: When you next pass on something that matters to the people you belong to, hear it first the way the one across from you will hear it — then hand it over at that size, and no more.
cells.core:
You pass things on and the passing changes them. Stories, customs, a phrase your family uses — they go through you and come out with your heat in them. That's not distortion. That's what keeps meaning alive, and you do it in plain view.
Because you're steady about it, you can hold two things true at once: what was handed to you, and what this moment actually needs. When both are in your hands, what you say lands, and the ones listening lean toward it. Hold that. The next time you carry something worth carrying, hear it first the way the one across from you will hear it, then give it at that size.
cells.sheetLine: You hand meaning on and it comes out alive.
cells.verb: carrying a piece of shared meaning forward and setting it alight
cells.place: where meaning is handed down between people and rituals keep what proved worth keeping

cells.tense: You will build the change into the tradition, and until it is built there is no rest in it.
cells.act: build the change by persistent work
cells.ask: For the next month, break ground on the change you want in how your people keep this. Work it slowly, without stopping, and let a month pass before you check whether it moved.
cells.core:
The version in your head is better than the one on the table. So you push the table toward it. You push fast, at the ones who keep it with you, at the ritual, at how your people say things. The vision holds. The pace is outrunning what anyone can carry, and the ones sharing this with you can feel it arriving ahead of its time.
What is actually yours to do is slower and duller than the vision. Break ground on the change you want, and work it slowly for a month without stopping, no looking to see if it moved until the month is up. Undramatic, and it holds. The rest of the version in your head can wait its turn.
cells.sheetLine: You want the whole change now. Break ground slowly instead.

cells.tense: You were the one who used to carry this, and you have not come back to the table.
cells.act: reason it through fast and cleanly
cells.ask: Follow the custom you keep circling, on paper, until it reaches its sharpest point. Take it as far as it goes in one sitting, then put the pen down. No one sees it.
cells.core:
Something you used to carry — a ritual, a story, a way your people have of doing things — and you stand outside it now. You watch it happen and say nothing. You still know it well. You just don't lift it anymore. The part of you that handed meaning to others has gone quiet, and the quiet has grown comfortable.
Feeling won't do this. Thinking will. Follow the custom you keep circling, on paper, until it reaches its sharpest point — in one sitting, as far as it goes. Then put the pen down. You don't need to hand it to anyone, and nobody sees what you wrote. Just see where it lands.
cells.sheetLine: You carry nothing now, and you keep circling it.

cells.tense: You are already writing what these people hold, and you have not put your name to it.
cells.act: say the hard thing gently, once
cells.ask: When a moment comes this week and your people are headed somewhere untrue, say it — gently, once, then let it go. Choose the moment. Say it as yours, and hold nothing after it.
cells.core:
You shape what this group holds. A correction made before anyone names it, a story told a little truer than it was, an old practice quietly adjusted — and asked, you'd say it just went that way. The shaping is happening. Your hand is on it. You file it under the times changing, and the ones beside you don't.
What's missing is only that you know it. When a moment comes this week and your people are headed somewhere untrue, say so — gently, once, then let it go. Choose the moment. Not as a correction somebody else should have made. As something true, and yours.

attempts.check: The status is a condition of one capacity in one part of a life, not proof of anyone's history or feelings; where a cell reads like a person's whole character rather than this capacity in this seat, narrow the claim. A reader could object that a strong urge to change a tradition, or a holding back from one, is simply good judgment rather than excess or depletion — the ask survives that, because handing something down and pausing before you speak are useful regardless of the diagnosis. The sentence that serves me more than them is any line where the reader is told what they really feel underneath; cut those and keep only what they could recognize and answer back to.
